hierarchy.reason: The workbench creates one dominant proof statement and gives the rail a clear reading start without adding competing card headlines.

composition.reason: The open rail uses controlled item widths, structural separators and a visible next-item cue. Compact recomposition removes the narrow-column failure.

pacing.reason: Quote length, portrait pause and the control row create deliberate reading rhythm; the page does not add ornamental sections.

typography.reason: One sans family and a narrow role hierarchy keep emphasis on supplied testimony. Quote-only does not introduce a new display style.

productTruth.reason: All eight live testimonials are present, seven real prepared clips render through CMP-05 and Daniel's absent clip is represented honestly.

distinctiveness.reason: Live halftone people in a borderless editorial proof rail are recognisably Mez without gradients, glass, card stacks or template chrome.

narrative.reason: The workbench moves from real operator proof to measured implementation facts, then ends with the open human gate.

conversionClarity.reason: This component has no conversion CTA by design; the interaction intent is nevertheless explicit through named controls, status and scroll instruction.

emotionalResonance.reason: Moving human portraits and unedited operator language create warmth without manufactured proof theatre.

craft.reason: Focus, keyboard endpoints, source resolution, quote-only state, reduced motion and offscreen idling are resolved as one coherent contract.

originality.reason: The candidate rejects the expected endless marquee and glossy testimonial-card pattern in favour of an evidence-led, user-driven reading rail.

T1StripTest.method: The rendered surface was inspected in its native monochrome state. It contains no gradient, glow, texture or colour dependency; greyscale neutralisation does not change hierarchy.
T1StripTest.evidence: The workbench remains legible through scale, spacing, hairlines and type alone.

T2ComponentRepetitionTest.method: Adjacent workbench sections and repeated item anatomy were inspected at desktop and compact widths.
T2ComponentRepetitionTest.evidence: The testimonial proof rail, measurement table and editorial gate note use different composition families. Repeated testimonial items share only the minimal semantic carrier required for a replaceable future card.

T3MotionComparisonTest.method: Two visible portrait crops were captured 1,250 ms apart and compared at an 8-level RGB threshold; track scrollLeft was independently sampled without commands.
T3MotionComparisonTest.evidence: 5,685 of 41,000 portrait pixels changed (13.87%) while uncommanded track drift remained 0 px. Motion adds human presence; it does not move the reading rail.

T4RealContentTest.method: The workbench used the live AI OS quotes, names and handles with the seven prepared repository portrait clips; no placeholder content was substituted.
T4RealContentTest.evidence: Long and short quotes, seven portraits and Daniel's real quote-only state all remained coherent from 320 through 1440.

canonScan.notes: No mesh gradient, indigo-violet palette, glass treatment, ambient shadow, backdrop blur, generic dashboard shell or AI-style decorative filler appears in the candidate.

humanGate.question: Does Olli want to promote this deliberately minimal proof rail before supplying his future testimonial-card anatomy?
